A lean amber-skinned fae with cropped violet hair and beetle-iridescent wings in a scarlet petal-silk tunic who races standing on her thwart, arms wide; a stout laughing elder with silver braids and moth-dusted wings in moss-velvet who rows sitting backwards and wins anyway; and a bright scattered field in plum, marigold and cream, a snail keeping pace along the bank ahead of them all.

A freckled pale fae with long copper plaits and birch-seed wings in a single-leaf tunic who cheats by blowing her rivals' sails inside-out with one sharp breath and grins; a grave tall one in bark-fibre with dragonfly-clear wings who never glances sideways; and a loose field of young fae in woven grass, bare feet braced, sleeves pushed to the elbow.

Two brown-skinned sisters with wild black hair and matching butterfly-patterned wings in moss-velvet kilted at the knee who bicker the entire length of the course and still cross together; a tiny ancient fae in an acorn-cup cap who steers by leaning and arrives first; and the rest bright as scattered berries behind.

A heavyset dark-skinned fae with close-cropped silver hair and iridescent wings rowing a hull three times too wide for him in deep plum bark-fibre, perfectly calm; a whip-thin young one in marigold petal-silk with moth-soft wings who is plainly terrified and holding the mast with both fists; and a varied field of fae in leaf-cloth and woven grass strung out behind, a walnut-shell mouse-tender towed as ballast catching every eye.

A golden-skinned fae with a long auburn braid and clear dragonfly wings in rose petal-silk who steers with one bare foot and never looks at the water; a small cool-toned one in woven grass with birch-seed wings who cheats by reading the current three bends ahead; and behind them a cheerful scatter in scarlet, cream and deep green, wings every kind.

A very small pale fae with white-blonde ringlets and moth-dusted wings in a cloak of overlapping violet petals, clearly racing a hull far too big, bailing with an acorn cap as she goes; a long-limbed dark one in plum leaf-cloth who poles from the stern with impossible elegance; and a field of fae from the very young to the silver-haired in every warm and cool tone, all barefoot.

A calm brown-eyed fae with close-cropped dark hair and beetle-iridescent wings in moss-green bark-fibre who never hurries and keeps arriving first, expression unreadable; a wild-haired ginger fae in scarlet petal-silk with butterfly wings who is reckless and wonderful and permanently soaking wet; and a loose bright crowd behind them in marigold, plum and cream, wings catching the spray.

A stout cheerful fae with long silver hair loose in the wind and moth-soft wings in deep teal moss-velvet who rows sitting backwards and shouts advice at racers she has already lapped; a cool-toned young one in woven grass with birch-seed wings, first race, knuckles white; and the field behind a scatter of berry-red, amber and pale gold, a dandelion seed doing duty as a spare sail on the last hull in line.

A tall grave dark-skinned fae with a heavy black plait and dragonfly-clear wings in a plum bark-fibre tunic who sails standing silent in the bow; a small warm-toned one in an acorn-cup cap and ivy-green leaf-cloth who cheats charmingly by leaning into other boats; and a varied field of fae in petal-silk and woven grass, wing-kinds ranging from iridescent to moth-dusted.

A pair of copper-skinned cousins sharing one grass-cord paddle, their red-brown hair tangled together, butterfly wings out of phase, both laughing and neither steering; a silver-haired elder in deep scarlet moss-velvet with beetle wings who watches them with fond despair and overtakes; and behind a bright staggered field in cream, marigold and plum, every build from slight to broad.

A reckless pale-skinned fae with short dark hair and iridescent wings in a tunic cut from one ivy leaf who steers into the fastest water with her eyes shut and always survives; a broad warm-toned one in amber petal-silk with moth-dusted wings rowing with immense calm; and a field of young and old fae behind in leaf-cloth and bark-fibre, a boot-shaped seed-pod among them bailed dry with one acorn cap.

A lean cool-toned fae with long silver-white hair and birch-seed wings in pale moss-velvet who navigates by watching the ripple ahead of the ripple and wins in silence; a freckled red-haired young one in marigold petal-silk with clear wings who is enormously confident and entirely wrong about her line; and a joyful varied field behind in rose, plum and bark-fibre.

A round-faced young fae with tight dark curls and soft moth-wings in a cloak of overlapping rose petals, visibly surprised to still be upright; a heavyset elder with cropped grey hair and iridescent wings in deep plum bark-fibre who races a hull twice her size with magnificent stubbornness; and a bright field of fae behind in woven grass and petal-silk, all bare-footed, a beetle stowed under one thwart watching proceedings.

A dark-skinned fae with long silver braids and clear dragonfly wings in scarlet petal-silk who cheats by reading the wind off a heron's wing and blames no one; a tiny pale one in woven grass with birch-seed wings who is terrified and racing anyway, chin up; and the field behind them a loose weave of marigold, moss-green and cream.

A broad golden-skinned fae with auburn hair braided tight and moth-dusted wings in deep green leaf-cloth who rows sitting backwards and keeps winning, mystifying everyone; a thin young one in plum petal-silk with butterfly wings standing on his thwart for a better view of the wrong bend; and a mixed field in bark-fibre and woven grass, young to silver-haired, wings every shape.

A very small silver-haired fae with warm brown skin and iridescent wings in a single-petal tunic of deep rose who steers by leaning left and always makes it work; a tall cool-toned one in bark-fibre with dragonfly wings who is reckless in a slow, deliberate, unstoppable way; and a scatter of fae behind in cream, marigold and plum, a snail on the bank maintaining a quiet lead.

A freckled pale fae with wild copper hair and birch-seed wings in an amber petal-silk tunic kilted above the knee who cheats by catching another boat's wake and grins wide; a stout dark-skinned elder in teal moss-velvet with moth-soft wings who never rushes and is already three lengths ahead; and behind them a bright crowd in leaf-cloth and woven grass, bare feet, sleeves rolled.

Two tall warm-toned fae with long black hair and matching dragonfly-clear wings in moss-velvet who have been bickering since the start and will still be bickering at the finish, every stroke a negotiation; a calm small one in cream petal-silk with birch-seed wings who slips past them in the argument; and a varied field behind in plum, berry-red and gold.

A golden-skinned fae with close-cropped white hair and iridescent wings in deep plum bark-fibre who is racing a hull twice her arm-span with total concentration; a whip-thin young one in rose petal-silk with butterfly wings who has capsized twice and is still going, soaking, laughing; and the field behind a joyful scatter in marigold, moss-green and cream, a mouse in a walnut shell towed at the rear drawing all the onlookers.

A lean dark-skinned fae with long auburn locs and moth-dusted wings in woven grass, sleeves pushed back, rowing with her eyes closed and trusting the current; a stout pale elder with silver hair loose and beetle-iridescent wings in scarlet leaf-cloth who shouts rhythmic encouragement at everyone he passes; and a bright field behind in bark-fibre and petal-silk, young to ancient.

A small cool-toned fae with white-blonde hair and clear wings in a violet petal-silk tunic who steers by leaning one knee on the rail and watching the far reed-bed; a heavyset warm-toned one in moss-velvet with moth-soft wings who cheats by knowing every eddy from childhood; and a loose field of fae behind in plum, marigold and cream, a dandelion seed deployed as a racing sail on the smallest hull.

A freckled brown-skinned fae with short red hair and butterfly wings in a cloak of overlapping yellow petals who is reckless and magnificent, hull at forty-five degrees the whole way; a grave silver-haired one in plum bark-fibre with dragonfly-clear wings who races in perfect silence and perfect stillness; and the varied field behind, a bright stagger of green, amber and rose, wings catching light.

A tall pale fae with long dark hair plaited twice and birch-seed wings in deep green leaf-cloth who cheats by blowing ripples across her rivals' bows and looks serene; a tiny dark-skinned one in an acorn-cup cap and woven grass, clearly terrified, hands gripping both sides of the hull, still going; and a cheerful field behind in scarlet, cream and marigold.

A stout dark-skinned fae with close-cropped grey hair and iridescent wings in a rose petal-silk tunic who never sits down and never stops talking; a lean young one in amber moss-velvet with moth-dusted wings who is absolutely calm and approximately twelve lengths ahead; and a field of fae behind in woven grass and bark-fibre, every warm and cool skin tone, a boot-shaped seed-pod bailed cheerfully with an acorn cap mid-race.

A pair of silver-haired elders with warm brown skin and matching beetle wings in complementary plum and teal bark-fibre who have been bickering about the best line since before anyone else was born; a tiny young pale fae in scarlet petal-silk with birch-seed wings who squeezes between them in the argument and takes the bend; and a bright loose field behind in marigold, rose and cream.
